speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I need to understand your chest skin lesion better; can you tell me how long you have had it and if it is changing in size, color, or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (cSCC). The patient is a 63-year-old male with a 2-month history of an increasing chest lesion, no pain/itch, and significant risk factors including age and diabetes. This clinical picture is highly suspicious for malignancy.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest lesion dermoscopy and full-body skin exam.
